// Built-in node:sqlite adapter — available in Node >= 22.5.0.
// No native build, no npm install. API mirrors betterSqliteAdapter.
import { PRAGMA_SQL } from "../schema.js";

const CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_MS = 60 * 1000;

export async function createNodeSqliteAdapter(filePath) {
  // Suppress "ExperimentalWarning: SQLite is an experimental feature" from node:sqlite.
  // Stable enough for production use as of Node 22.x (RC quality).
  const origEmit = process.emit;
  process.emit = function (name, data, ...rest) {
    if (name === "warning" && data?.name === "ExperimentalWarning" && /SQLite/i.test(data.message || "")) {
      return false;
    }
    return origEmit.call(process, name, data, ...rest);

## ✅ Per-Commit UI Verification — Complete Report

I built a full E2E environment (packaged **0.5.75** app on port 20130 + mock OpenAI upstream on 24000) and manually exercised **every UI function added by each commit**, including cross-effects on other parts of the app.

- **Test button** → ECONNREFUSED → "Proxy test failed" toast, pool marked error/inactive, "Last tested: … connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:7897"

### 2. `063ee9c0` + `104ecf75` — Messages (facets, identity, annotations, actions, hooks) ✅

- **Actions menu**: Copy cURL, Export JSON, Replay, Summarize, webhook, note, tag, alert-on-match — all present

// Concurrency stress test — simulate many parallel saveRequestUsage / saveRequestDetail
// to verify atomic counter, no data loss, no race conditions.
import fs from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll, afterAll, vi } from "vitest";

const originalDataDir = process.env.DATA_DIR;
let tempDir;
let db;

beforeAll(async () => {
  tempDir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "9router-concurrent-"));
  process.env.DATA_DIR = tempDir;
  vi.resetModules();
  db = await import("@/lib/db/index.js");
  await db.initDb();
});

afterAll(() => {
  if (tempDir) fs.rmSync(tempDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  if (originalDataDir === undefined) delete process.env.DATA_DIR;
  else process.env.DATA_DIR = originalDataDir;
});

import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { getSavedViews, saveView, deleteSavedView } from "@/lib/usageDb";

/**
 * GET /api/saved-views
 * List saved filter presets.
 * Response: { views: [{ id, name, filter, createdAt, updatedAt }] }
 */
export async function GET() {
  try {
    const views = await getSavedViews();
    return NextResponse.json({ views });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[API] Failed to get saved views:", error);
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "Failed to fetch saved views" }, { status: 500 });
  }
}

/**
 * POST /api/saved-views
 * Create or update a saved view (upsert by name).
 * Body: { name: string, filter: object }
 * Response: { view: {...} }
 */
export async function POST(request) {
  try {
    const body = await request.json().catch(() => ({}));
    const { name, filter } = body;
    if (!name || !filter) {
      return NextResponse.json({ error: "name and filter are required" }, { status: 400 });
    }
    const view = await saveView({ name, filter });
    return NextResponse.json({ view }, { status: 201 });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[API] Failed to save view:", error);
    return NextResponse.json({ error: error.message || "Failed to save view" }, { status: 400 });
  }
}

/**
 * DELETE /api/saved-views?id=123 (or ?name=...)
 * Response: { deleted: true }
 */
export async function DELETE(request) {
  try {
    const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url);
    const id = searchParams.get("id");
    const name = searchParams.get("name");
    const deleted = await deleteSavedView({ id: id ? Number(id) : undefined, name: name || undefined });
    if (!deleted) {
      return NextResponse.json({ error: "Saved view not found" }, { status: 404 });
    }
    return NextResponse.json({ deleted: true });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[API] Failed to delete saved view:", error);
    return NextResponse.json({ error: error.message || "Failed to delete saved view" }, { status: 400 });
  }

/**
 * Delete a saved view by id or name.
 * @returns {Promise<boolean>} true if a row was deleted
 */
export async function deleteSavedView({ id, name } = {}) {
  const db = await getAdapter();
  if (id !== undefined) {
    const res = db.run(`DELETE FROM saved_views WHERE id = ?`, [id]);
    return res?.changes > 0;
  }
  if (name) {
    const res = db.run(`DELETE FROM saved_views WHERE name = ?`, [name]);
    return res?.changes > 0;
  }
  throw new Error("deleteSavedView requires id or name");

"use client";

import { useState, useEffect, useCallback } from "react";
import { getCapabilitiesForModel } from "open-sse/providers/capabilities.js";

// Module cache: one /api/models fetch shared by every useModelCaps instance.
let cache = null; // { byFull, byId } | null
let inflight = null;

function buildMaps(models) {
  const byFull = {};
  const byId = {};
  for (const m of models || []) {
    if (!m.caps) continue;
    if (m.fullModel) byFull[m.fullModel] = m.caps;
    if (m.routedModel) byFull[m.routedModel] = m.caps;
    if (m.model) byId[m.model] = m.caps;
  }
  return { byFull, byId };
}

function loadModelCaps() {
  if (cache) return Promise.resolve(cache);
  if (inflight) return inflight;
  inflight = fetch("/api/models")
    .then(async (res) => {
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`models ${res.status}`);
      const data = await res.json();
      cache = buildMaps(data.models);
      return cache;
    })
    .catch(() => {
      // Keep null so a later mount can retry
      return { byFull: {}, byId: {} };
    })
    .finally(() => { inflight = null; });
  return inflight;
}

// Resolve caps from a "provider/model" string or a bare model id.
function resolveCaps(byFull, byId, key) {
  if (!key) return null;
  if (byFull[key]) return byFull[key];
  const bare = key.includes("/") ? key.slice(key.indexOf("/") + 1) : key;
  if (byId[bare]) return byId[bare];
  const provider = key.includes("/") ? key.slice(0, key.indexOf("/")) : null;
  const c = getCapabilitiesForModel(provider, bare);
  return {
    vision: c.vision,
    search: c.search,
    reasoning: c.reasoning,
    contextWindow: c.contextWindow,
    maxOutput: c.maxOutput,
  };
}

export function useModelCaps() {
  const [byFull, setByFull] = useState(() => cache?.byFull || {});
  const [byId, setById] = useState(() => cache?.byId || {});

  useEffect(() => {
    let alive = true;
    const sync = (maps) => {
      if (alive) { setByFull(maps.byFull); setById(maps.byId); }
    };
    if (cache) {
      sync(cache);
    } else {
      loadModelCaps().then(sync);
    }
    // Custom models change at runtime — drop the shared cache and refetch
    const invalidate = () => {
      cache = null;
      loadModelCaps().then(sync);
    };
    window.addEventListener("customModelChanged", invalidate);
    return () => {
      alive = false;
      window.removeEventListener("customModelChanged", invalidate);
    };
  }, []);

  const getCaps = useCallback(
    (key) => resolveCaps(byFull, byId, key),
    [byFull, byId],
  );

  return { getCaps };
}

GAPS:
1. **backupDbLite root cause misdiagnosed**: The issue isn't just `exec()` support—it's that **SQLite forbids ATTACH DATABASE inside a transaction**. The `adapter.transaction()` wrapper creates a SAVEPOINT, which causes ATTACH to fail silently or throw. Your proposed fix should explicitly remove the transaction wrapper AND rewrite without ATTACH (since node:sqlite may not support ATTACH at all).
2. **Missing implementation detail for backupDbLite rewrite**: Your plan says "copy schema and data table-by-table" but doesn't specify how to handle indexes, triggers, and views. The current code has a `// copy indexes...` comment that needs fleshing out. The rewrite must copy all schema objects, not just tables.
3. **Test helper flush must be awaited**: Your plan says "call flushRequestDetails() after the 120ms sleep" but doesn't emphasize that it must be `await`ed. If the test helper doesn't await the flush, the race condition persists.
4. **Other tests may be affected**: You haven't verified whether other test files also rely on the 120ms sleep pattern. If they do, they'll need the same fix. A grep for `sleep(120)` or similar patterns in the test suite is needed.
5. **Production code flush timing**: You asked if `saveRequestDetail` should flush immediately—the answer is **no**. The 5s buffer is intentional for performance. But you should verify that no production code paths depend on immediate visibility (e.g., UI code that saves then immediately queries). If such paths exist, they need to call `flushRequestDetails()` explicitly.

RECOMMENDED_PLAN:
1. **Failures 1 & 3 (test flush timing)**:
   - Update the test's `saveDetail` helper to `await flushRequestDetails()` after calling `saveRequestDetail()`. Remove or reduce the 120ms sleep since it's no longer needed.
   - Grep the entire test suite for similar patterns (e.g., `sleep(120)` after `saveDetail`) and apply the same fix to all affected tests.
   - Verify that no production code calls `saveRequestDetail()` then immediately queries the database. If such code exists, add explicit `await flushRequestDetails()` calls there.

2. **Failure 2 (backupDbLite)**:
   - Rewrite `backupDbLite` to **avoid ATTACH DATABASE entirely**. Instead:
     - Create a new SQLite connection to the backup file using the adapter's constructor or a direct `better-sqlite3` import.
     - For each table (excluding `requestDetails`), fetch its schema from `sqlite_master`, execute the CREATE TABLE on the backup connection, then copy data with `INSERT INTO backup.table SELECT * FROM main.table` (using the two connections).
     - Copy all indexes, triggers, and views by querying `sqlite_master` for `type='index'`, `type='trigger'`, `type='view'` and executing their SQL on the backup connection.
   - Remove the `adapter.transaction()` wrapper since it's unnecessary when not using ATTACH.
   - Add error handling to ensure the backup file is cleaned up if the copy fails mid-way.

3. **Validation**:
   - Run the full test suite to ensure no regressions from the flush timing changes.
   - Manually test `backupDbLite` with a database containing tables, indexes, triggers, and views to verify all schema objects are copied correctly.
   - Verify that the backup file can be opened and queried successfully after the backup operation.

## 🔴 IDOR CONFIRMED on `/api/keys/[id]` — live proof on mini4:20129

Just ran the 4-step probe against the fresh build (PID 49092):

| Step | What I did | What came back |
|---|---|---|
| 1. `GET /api/keys` (list) | Auth'd, list all keys | `sk-cb9••••••••••••••••••••••••1a0b` (**masked** ✅) |
| 2. Login fresh | Get session cookie | `{"success":true}` |
| 3. List again | Extract UUID | `b0c998da-e0a4-498d-a266-c81284c62f7e` |
| 4. `GET /api/keys/` | Single-key endpoint | **`sk-cb9c2fba45e06923-d3yviq-12f51a0b`** (**RAW, UNMASKED** 🔴) |

The list endpoint does the right thing (masks), but the single-key GET hands back the full credential to anyone who knows the UUID — and the list endpoint hands out the UUID freely.

**Attack surface on this box alone:** any LAN peer who can load the dashboard can see the masked list → copy the UUID → curl the single-key endpoint → steal the key. In SSO/multi-user deployments this scales to any authenticated peer.

**PUT and DELETE are even worse:** same route, same ID-only lookup, no owner/auth check — any authenticated session can toggle, rename, or revoke any key on the system.

## ✅ aria-hidden fix proved working in production

Playwright probe on the same fresh build returned for 8 nav links:

```
verdict: "ARIA-HIDDEN WORKING"
```

All sidebar nav `<a>` elements now have their inner `.material-symbols-outlined` span with `aria-hidden="true"`. Screen readers will announce just "Endpoint & Key" instead of "api Endpoint & Key".

## What I'd do next (pending your go-ahead)

The IDOR needs a fix that changes API behavior, so I won't ship it autonomously. Two options:

### Option A — Minimal fix (5 min, backward-compat for dashboard)
- Mask `key` field on `GET /api/keys/[id]` the same way list does
- Add `requireAuth(request)` check at top of PUT/DELETE to reject non-browser sessions
- Dashboard keeps working (it already has the full key from POST create flow); only the IDOR leak closes

### Option B — Proper fix (15 min, tighter security model)
- All of Option A, **plus**
- Scope every key operation to the current session's keys (owner-based access control)
- Add a `revealFullKey` POST endpoint with a one-time token for the dashboard's copy-to-clipboard flow
- Full audit of other `[id]` routes (providers, combos, etc.) for the same pattern

**Say A or B** and I'll implement + prove + rebuild. Or point me at something else from your mini2 probes.

# Status — `v5-vscode-works @ 7c611d7c` (12 commits)

## Just landed (commit `7c611d7c`)
**Link-local / cloud-metadata SSRF guard** for user-controllable `baseUrl` paths.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/shared/utils/ssrfGuard.js` | Added `assertNotLinkLocal` + `assertNotLinkLocalResolved` (sync + DNS-rebinding) |
| `src/app/api/providers/[id]/test/testUtils.js` | OpenAI-compat + Anthropic-compat + llm7 branches guarded |
| `src/app/api/providers/validate/route.js` | OpenAI-compat + custom-embedding + Anthropic-compat branches guarded |
| `tests/unit/provider-ssrf-link-local.test.js` | 27 tests, all green |

**Design decision (the non-obvious part):**
- **NOT** the existing `assertPublicUrlResolved` — that would have broken production Ollama at `localhost:11434`, LAN vLLM boxes at `192.168.x/10.x`, and Tailscale CGNAT at `100.64/10` (confirmed in deployment-runbook + SESSION-HISTORY as real production traffic on mini2).
- **Only** blocks `169.254.0.0/16` + `fe80::/10` — the one IP class that is *never* a legitimate model host (AWS/GCP/Azure metadata `169.254.169.254`, ECS task metadata `169.254.170.2`, IPv6 link-local).
- DNS-rebinding covered: non-literal hostnames resolved via `dns.promises.lookup` before the check, so attacker-owned domains pointed at metadata IPs are also caught.

mini4 is confirmed clean (zero evil rows, zero evil.example.com in settings, zero providerConnections rows). But I need to correct something important: my earlier checkpoint wrongly called the mini2 `settings.data` evil match a "JWT false positive." The actual evidence shows it's a **stored XSS test artifact** — `settings.data → $.smartRouter.evil_key = "<script>alert(416)</script>"`. That's a real evil artifact that still needs purging.

Let me surgically remove it without touching the password hash or other settings, then verify.<tool_name>run_in_terminal</tool_name>
<explanation>Surgically remove the stored-XSS test artifact $.smartRouter.evil_key from settings.data via json_remove, preserving all other settings (password hash, smartRouter.enabled/names, etc.), then verify, WAL-checkpoint, integrity-check, and confirm app health.</explanation>
<goal>Stage 6c: purge stored-XSS evil_key from mini2 settings.data</goal>
<mode>sync</mode>
<timeout>30000</timeout>
<command>export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin"; ssh -F /dev/null -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 chris@100.96.109.61 bash -s <<'REMOTE'
DB=~/.9router/db/data.sqlite
echo "=== BEFORE: smartRouter.evil_key value ==="
sqlite3 "$DB" "SELECT json_extract(data,'\$.smartRouter.evil_key') FROM settings WHERE id=1;"
echo
echo "=== BEFORE: full smartRouter object ==="
sqlite3 "$DB" "SELECT json_extract(data,'\$.smartRouter') FROM settings WHERE id=1;"
echo
echo "=== SURGICAL json_remove of \$.smartRouter.evil_key only ==="
sqlite3 "$DB" "UPDATE settings SET data = json_remove(data, '\$.smartRouter.evil_key') WHERE id=1; SELECT changes() AS rows_updated;"
echo
echo "=== AFTER: evil_key (should be empty/null) ==="
sqlite3 "$DB" "SELECT json_extract(data,'\$.smartRouter.evil_key') FROM settings WHERE id=1;"
echo "(blank above = removed)"
echo
echo "=== AFTER: smartRouter object still intact? ==="
sqlite3 "$DB" "SELECT json_extract(data,'\$.smartRouter') FROM settings WHERE id=1;"
echo
echo "=== AFTER: password hash still present (untouched)? ==="
sqlite3 "$DB" "SELECT substr(json_extract(data,'\$.password'),1,10) || '...(preserved)' FROM settings WHERE id=1;"
echo
echo "=== AFTER: total 'evil' count in settings.data (must be 0) ==="
sqlite3 "$DB" "SELECT (length(data) - length(replace(data,'evil',''))) / 4 AS evil_count FROM settings WHERE id=1;"
echo
echo "=== WAL checkpoint ==="
sqlite3 "$DB" "PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE);"
echo
echo "=== integrity ==="
sqlite3 "$DB" "PRAGMA integrity_check;"
echo
echo "=== app health after settings mutation ==="
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "mini2_health=%{http_code}\n" --max-time 5 http://localhost:20128/api/health
echo
echo "=== FINAL: any 'evil' left in providerConnections OR settings across both tables ==="
sqlite3 "$DB" "SELECT 'providerConnections', count(*) FROM providerConnections WHERE data LIKE '%evil%' OR name LIKE '%evil%' UNION ALL SELECT 'settings', count(*) FROM settings WHERE data LIKE '%evil.example.com%';"
REMOTE</command>
</tool>

3. Test the validator module directly<tool_name>create_file</tool_name>
<code>
/**
 * Provider overrides header validation.
 *
 * SECURITY (Row 19, 2026-10-27): Shared validation logic for provider header
 * overrides. Both PATCH /api/settings and PUT /api/providers/[id]/overrides
 * must apply this gate to prevent authenticated users from injecting
 * security-sensitive headers (Authorization, Host, Cookie, forwarding headers)
 * that would be sent on every upstream request via base.js:132.
 *
 * @param {object} providerOverrides - The providerOverrides object from request body
 * @returns {{ ok: boolean, error?: string }}
 */

const MAX_HEADERS = 20;
const MAX_HEADER_VALUE_LENGTH = 8192;
const HEADER_NAME_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$/;

// Headers that must never be overridden — structure/auth/forwarding headers
// that would compromise request integrity or enable header injection attacks.
const BLOCKED_HEADERS = new Set([
  // Request structure
  "host", "content-length", "content-type", "connection", "transfer-encoding",
  // Auth
  "authorization", "cookie",
  // Forwarding / trust / peer headers (defense-in-depth against Bug GG variants)
  "x-forwarded-for", "x-forwarded-host", "x-forwarded-proto",
  "x-forwarded-server", "x-real-ip", "x-original-host", "x-real-host",
  "x-9r-real-ip", "x-9r-peer-token", "x-9r-via-proxy",
]);

export function validateProviderOverrides(providerOverrides) {
  if (providerOverrides === null || providerOverrides === undefined) {
    return { ok: true };
  }

  if (typeof providerOverrides !== "object" || Array.isArray(providerOverrides)) {
    return { ok: false, error: "providerOverrides must be an object" };
  }

  for (const [providerId, override] of Object.entries(providerOverrides)) {
    if (override === null || override === undefined) continue;

    if (typeof override !== "object" || Array.isArray(override)) {
      return {
        ok: false,
        error: `providerOverrides.${providerId} must be an object`,
      };
    }

    const headers = override.headers;
    if (headers === undefined || headers === null) continue;

    if (typeof headers !== "object" || Array.isArray(headers)) {
      return {
        ok: false,
        error: `providerOverrides.${providerId}.headers must be an object`,
      };
    }

    const entries = Object.entries(headers).filter(([, v]) => v !== "" && v != null);

    if (entries.length > MAX_HEADERS) {
      return {
        ok: false,
        error: `providerOverrides.${providerId}: too many headers (max ${MAX_HEADERS})`,
      };
    }

    for (const [name, value] of entries) {
      if (!HEADER_NAME_RE.test(name)) {
        return {
          ok: false,
          error: `providerOverrides.${providerId}: invalid header name '${name}'`,
        };
      }

      if (typeof value !== "string" || /[\r\n]/.test(value)) {
        return {
          ok: false,
          error: `providerOverrides.${providerId}: invalid value for header '${name}'`,
        };
      }

      if (value.length > MAX_HEADER_VALUE_LENGTH) {
        return {
          ok: false,
          error: `providerOverrides.${providerId}: header '${name}' value too long (max ${MAX_HEADER_VALUE_LENGTH})`,
        };
      }

      if (BLOCKED_HEADERS.has(name.toLowerCase())) {
        return {
          ok: false,
</tool_invoke>
          error: `providerOverrides.${providerId}: header '${name}' cannot be overridden`,
        };
      }
    }
  }

  return { ok: true };
}
